Name: Genius
Description: Crowdsourced lyrics and music knowledge
Introduction: The Genius API is a powerful tool that provides access to one of the largest collections of musical and lyrical data on the internet. As a crowdsourced platform, Genius offers a comprehensive database of valuable content that contains verified annotations, lyrics, and insights contributed by a passionate community of enthusiasts. With the Genius API, developers can easily integrate these data sources into their applications and websites, providing users with a wealth of knowledge and context around their favorite music. The API offers a wide range of functions, including: 1) Searching the Genius database for specific songs, artists, or albums. 2) Retrieving detailed song information, including lyrics and annotations. 3) Accessing metadata information about artists and albums. 4) Enabling user authentication for personalized annotations and comments. With its rich set of features and massive database, the Genius API is an essential tool for any developer looking to create engaging music-related applications and experiences.
Functions:
1. Name: search
Description: This function allows users to search the Genius database for specific songs, artists, or albums.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- q: String. The search query.
- per_page: Integer. The number of results to return per page. Default is 20.
- page: Integer. The page number of the results to return. Default is 1.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a search result. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the search result.
- type: String. The type of the search result (song, artist, or album).
- title: String. The title of the search result.
- url: String. The URL of the search result on the Genius website.
- header_image_url: String. The URL of the header image for the search result.
- thumbnail_url: String. The URL of the thumbnail image for the search result.

2. Name: getSong
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific song, including lyrics and annotations.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the song.
Output: A JSON object representing the song. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the song.
- title: String. The title of the song.
- full_title: String. The full title of the song, including the artist name.
- artist: JSON object. The artist of the song. The object contains the following keys:
  - id: Integer. The Genius ID of the artist.
  - name: String. The name of the artist.
  - url: String. The URL of the artist on the Genius website.
- album: JSON object. The album of the song. The object contains the following keys:
  - id: Integer. The Genius ID of the album.
  - name: String. The name of the album.
  - url: String. The URL of the album on the Genius website.
- lyrics: String. The lyrics of the song.
- media: JSON object. The media associated with the song. The object contains the following keys:
  - provider: String. The provider of the media (e.g. YouTube).
  - url: String. The URL of the media.
- description: String. The description of the song.
- annotations: Array of JSON objects. The annotations associated with the song. Each object contains the following keys:
  - id: Integer. The Genius ID of the annotation.
  - body: String. The body of the annotation.
  - url: String. The URL of the annotation on the Genius website.
  - author: JSON object. The author of the annotation. The object contains the following keys:
    - id: Integer. The Genius ID of the author.
    - name: String. The name of the author.
    - url: String. The URL of the author on the Genius website.

3. Name: getArtist
Description: This function allows users to retrieve metadata information about a specific artist.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the artist.
Output: A JSON object representing the artist. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the artist.
- name: String. The name of the artist.
- url: String. The URL of the artist on the Genius website.
- header_image_url: String. The URL of the header image for the artist.
- image_url: String. The URL of the image for the artist.
- facebook_name: String. The Facebook name of the artist.
- twitter_name: String. The Twitter name of the artist.
- instagram_name: String. The Instagram name of the artist.
- description: String. The description of the artist.

4. Name: getAlbum
Description: This function allows users to retrieve metadata information about a specific album.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the album.
Output: A JSON object representing the album. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. The Genius ID of the album.
- name: String. The name of the album.
- url: String. The URL of the album on the Genius website.
- cover_art_url: String. The URL of the cover art for the album.
- artist: JSON object. The artist of the album. The object contains the following keys:
  - id: Integer. The Genius ID of the artist.
  - name: String. The name of the artist.
  - url: String. The URL of the artist on the Genius website.
- description: String. The description of the album.

5. Name: authenticate
Description: This function allows users to authenticate with the Genius API in order to access personalized annotations and comments.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- client_id: String. The client ID of the application.
- client_secret: String. The client secret of the application.
- code: String. The authorization code obtained from the user.
- redirect_uri: String. The redirect URI of the application.
Output: A JSON object representing the access token. The object contains the following keys:
- access_token: String. The access token for the authenticated user.
- token_type: String. The type of the access token.
- expires_in: Integer. The number of seconds until the access token expires.

Name: OpenAQ
Description: Open air quality data
Introduction: OpenAQ is an API (Application Programming Interface) that provides open data for air quality across the world. It provides the following functionalities to its users: 1) Retrieve a list of countries, cities, or locations with their respective air quality measurement data such as PM2.5 and PM10. 2) Filter the data by date range, coordinate, or pollutant type. 3) Get the latest measurement for a specific location. This API is useful for researchers, developers, and organizations that require up-to-date and accurate air quality data for their projects.
Functions:
1. Name: getCountries
    Description: Retrieve a list of countries with their respective ISO codes.
    Input: None
    Output: An array of objects, each object contains the following information:
            - country: string, the name of the country
            - code: string, the ISO code of the country

2. Name: getCities
    Description: Retrieve a list of cities with their respective air quality measurement data.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
            - country: string, the ISO code of the country where the cities are located
    Output: An array of objects, each object contains the following information:
            - city: string, the name of the city
            - count: integer, the number of locations with air quality data in the city
            - locations: array of objects, each object contains the following information:
                - location: string, the name of the location
                - count: integer, the number of measurements for the location

3. Name: getLocations
    Description: Retrieve a list of locations with their respective air quality measurement data.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
            - city: string, the name of the city where the locations are located
            - country: string, the ISO code of the country where the locations are located
    Output: An array of objects, each object contains the following information:
            - location: string, the name of the location
            - count: integer, the number of measurements for the location
            - parameters: array of strings, the pollutants measured at the location

4. Name: getLatest
    Description: Retrieve the latest air quality measurement for a specific location.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
            - city: string, the name of the city where the location is located
            - country: string, the ISO code of the country where the location is located
            - location: string, the name of the location
    Output: An object containing the following information:
            - location: string, the name of the location
            - city: string, the name of the city where the location is located
            - country: string, the ISO code of the country where the location is located
            - measurements: array of objects, each object contains the following information:
                - parameter: string, the pollutant measured
                - value: number, the measurement value
                - unit: string, the unit of measurement
                - lastUpdated: string, the date and time when the measurement was taken

5. Name: getData
    Description: Retrieve air quality measurement data for a specific location.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
            - city: string, the name of the city where the location is located
            - country: string, the ISO code of the country where the location is located
            - location: string, the name of the location
            - parameter: string, the pollutant to retrieve data for
            - date_from: string, the start date of the date range to retrieve data for (format: YYYY-MM-DD)
            - date_to: string, the end date of the date range to retrieve data for (format: YYYY-MM-DD)
    Output: An array of objects, each object contains the following information:
            - date: string, the date of the measurement (format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ)
            - value: number, the measurement value
            - unit: string, the unit of measurement
            - averagingPeriod: object, contains the following information:
                - value: number, the averaging period value
                - unit: string, the unit of the averaging period value

Name: CloudConvert
Description: Online file converter for audio, video, document, ebook, archive, image, spreadsheet, presentation
Introduction: CloudConvert API is an online file converter service that provides a wide range of functionalities to convert files in various formats, including audio, video, documents, ebooks, archives, images, spreadsheets, and presentations. This API allows developers to integrate CloudConvert functionalities into their applications seamlessly. The API offers the following functions: 1) Convert files to multiple formats with customized settings such as quality, resolution, and size. 2) Extract content from files such as text, images, and audio. 3) Merge multiple files into a single document. 4) Compress and decompress files. 5) Provide a detailed progress report for ongoing conversions. The API provides high-quality conversion, fast processing times and supports more than 200 formats.
Functions:
1. Name: Convert
Description: Convert a file to a specified format with customized settings.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "input": String. The URL or base64-encoded data of the input file.
- "output_format": String. The desired output format.
- "converter_options": Object. Customized settings for the conversion process.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. The unique identifier of the conversion task.
- "url": String. The URL to download the converted file.
- "expire_at": String. The expiration time of the conversion task.
- "percent": Integer. The percentage of the conversion progress.
- "message": String. The current status of the conversion task.

2. Name: Extract
Description: Extract content from a file such as text, images, and audio.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "input": String. The URL or base64-encoded data of the input file.
- "output_format": String. The desired output format.
- "converter_options": Object. Customized settings for the extraction process.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. The unique identifier of the extraction task.
- "url": String. The URL to download the extracted content.
- "expire_at": String. The expiration time of the extraction task.
- "percent": Integer. The percentage of the extraction progress.
- "message": String. The current status of the extraction task.

3. Name: Merge
Description: Merge multiple files into a single document.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "input": Array of objects. The list of files to be merged. Each object should have the following keys:
  - "filename": String. The name of the file.
  - "url": String. The URL or base64-encoded data of the file.
- "output_format": String. The desired output format.
- "converter_options": Object. Customized settings for the merging process.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. The unique identifier of the merging task.
- "url": String. The URL to download the merged file.
- "expire_at": String. The expiration time of the merging task.
- "percent": Integer. The percentage of the merging progress.
- "message": String. The current status of the merging task.

4. Name: Compress
Description: Compress a file into a specified format.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "input": String. The URL or base64-encoded data of the input file.
- "output_format": String. The desired output format.
- "converter_options": Object. Customized settings for the compression process.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. The unique identifier of the compression task.
- "url": String. The URL to download the compressed file.
- "expire_at": String. The expiration time of the compression task.
- "percent": Integer. The percentage of the compression progress.
- "message": String. The current status of the compression task.

5. Name: Get Task
Description: Retrieve the status of a conversion, extraction, merging, or compression task.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "task_id": String. The unique identifier of the task.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. The unique identifier of the task.
- "url": String. The URL to download the output file.
- "expire_at": String. The expiration time of the task.
- "percent": Integer. The percentage of the task progress.
- "message": String. The current status of the task.

Each function is specifically designed to provide a unique service that makes it easy for developers to use. The API provides structured data in JSON format, which can be used with various programming languages. Start using the Breaking Bad Quotes API and create a fun and interactive experience for your users.

- author: (string) The name of the character.
Output: The function will return a JSON object containing the following fields:
- count: (integer) The number of quotes by the specified character.

4. Name: getQuoteBySeries

- series: (string) The name of the TV series.

- quote: (string) The text of the quote.
- author: (string) The name of the character who said the quote.
- series: (string) The name of the TV series.

- series: (string) The name of the TV series.

- count: (integer) The number of quotes from the specified TV series.

Name: WhatJobs
Description: Job search engine
Introduction: The WhatJobs API is a powerful job search engine that provides partners with access to its extensive job database. It offers the following functions to help job seekers find suitable employment opportunities: 1) Search for jobs by keyword, location, category, and type. 2) View job details such as job title, job description, and company information. 3) Filter search results based on job duration, salary range, and job type. 4) Sign up for job alerts and receive emails when a job matching the criteria is posted. This API is easy to use and can help job seekers find employment opportunities that match their skills and qualifications.
Functions:
1. Name: searchJobs
Description: This function allows users to search for jobs based on specific criteria such as keyword, location, category, and type.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- keyword: String. The keyword to search for in job titles and descriptions.
- location: String. The location to search for jobs in.
- category: String. The job category to search for.
- type: String. The job type to search for (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
Output: An array of job objects, each containing the following information:
- jobTitle: String. The title of the job.
- jobDescription: String. The description of the job.
- company: String. The name of the company offering the job.
- location: String. The location of the job.
- salary: String. The salary range for the job.
- jobType: String. The type of job (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
- jobDuration: String. The duration of the job (e.g. permanent, temporary).

2. Name: getJobDetails
Description: This function allows users to view the details of a specific job.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- jobId: Integer. The ID of the job to retrieve details for.
Output: A job object containing the following information:
- jobTitle: String. The title of the job.
- jobDescription: String. The description of the job.
- company: String. The name of the company offering the job.
- location: String. The location of the job.
- salary: String. The salary range for the job.
- jobType: String. The type of job (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
- jobDuration: String. The duration of the job (e.g. permanent, temporary).

3. Name: filterJobs
Description: This function allows users to filter search results based on job duration, salary range, and job type.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- jobDuration: String. The duration of the job (e.g. permanent, temporary).
- salaryRange: String. The salary range for the job.
- jobType: String. The type of job (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
Output: An array of job objects, each containing the following information:
- jobTitle: String. The title of the job.
- jobDescription: String. The description of the job.
- company: String. The name of the company offering the job.
- location: String. The location of the job.
- salary: String. The salary range for the job.
- jobType: String. The type of job (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
- jobDuration: String. The duration of the job (e.g. permanent, temporary).

4. Name: createJobAlert
Description: This function allows users to sign up for job alerts and receive emails when a job matching the criteria is posted.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- email: String. The email address to send job alerts to.
- keyword: String. The keyword to search for in job titles and descriptions.
- location: String. The location to search for jobs in.
- category: String. The job category to search for.
- type: String. The job type to search for (e.g. full-time, part-time, contract).
Output: A success message indicating that the job alert has been created.

Name: SpaceX
Description: Company, vehicle, launchpad and launch data
Introduction: The SpaceX API provides users with access to information about space exploration, space launches, and the SpaceX company. It offers several functions to provide users with a variety of data about SpaceX, its missions, and launch facilities. The functions offered by the SpaceX API include: 1) Company information including name, founder, and headquarters location. 2) Vehicle information, including type, description, and specifications. 3) Launchpad details, including the number of launches and total launch mass. 4) Launch data, including the details of each launch, including date and specific mission details. The API provides a convenient and reliable way for developers and space enthusiasts to stay up to date on the latest happenings in the world of space exploration.
Functions:
1. Name: getCompanyInfo
Description: Returns information about the SpaceX company.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
- name: String. The name of the company.
- founder: String. The name of the company's founder.
- founded: Integer. The year the company was founded.
- employees: Integer. The number of employees at the company.
- headquarters: Object. The location of the company's headquarters, including the address, city, state, and country.

2. Name: getVehicleInfo
Description: Returns information about SpaceX vehicles.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of vehicle objects, each with the following information:
- id: String. The unique identifier for the vehicle.
- name: String. The name of the vehicle.
- type: String. The type of vehicle (e.g. rocket, capsule).
- active: Boolean. Indicates whether the vehicle is currently active.
- description: String. A brief description of the vehicle.
- first_flight: String. The date of the vehicle's first flight.
- height: Object. The height of the vehicle, including meters and feet.
- diameter: Object. The diameter of the vehicle, including meters and feet.
- mass: Object. The mass of the vehicle, including kg and lb.
- payload_weights: Array. An array of objects containing information about the vehicle's payload weight capacity, including kg and lb.

3. Name: getLaunchpadInfo
Description: Returns information about SpaceX launchpads.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of launchpad objects, each with the following information:
- id: String. The unique identifier for the launchpad.
- name: String. The name of the launchpad.
- full_name: String. The full name of the launchpad, including the location.
- status: String. The current status of the launchpad (e.g. active, retired).
- location: Object. The location of the launchpad, including the latitude and longitude.
- vehicles_launched: Array. An array of vehicle IDs that have been launched from the launchpad.
- attempted_launches: Integer. The number of attempted launches from the launchpad.
- successful_launches: Integer. The number of successful launches from the launchpad.
- total_launches: Integer. The total number of launches from the launchpad.
- details: String. Additional details about the launchpad.

4. Name: getLaunchInfo
Description: Returns information about SpaceX launches.
Input: 
- flight_number: Optional. Integer. The flight number of the launch.
- launch_year: Optional. Integer. The year of the launch.
- launch_success: Optional. Boolean. Indicates whether the launch was successful.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of launch objects, each with the following information:
- flight_number: Integer. The flight number of the launch.
- mission_name: String. The name of the mission.
- launch_year: Integer. The year of the launch.
- launch_date_utc: String. The date and time of the launch in UTC.
- launch_success: Boolean. Indicates whether the launch was successful.
- rocket: Object. Information about the rocket used in the launch, including the rocket ID, name, and type.
- payloads: Array. An array of payload objects, each with the payload ID, name, and type.

Name: ClickUp
Description: ClickUp is a robust, cloud-based project management tool for boosting productivity
Introduction: The ClickUp API is a versatile integration tool that allows developers to seamlessly connect ClickUp's project management features in their existing workflow. It provides the following functions: 1) Create and manage tasks, projects, workspaces, and teams. 2) Access task details, including comments, due dates, assignees, and custom fields. 3) Track time spent on tasks with integrations for various time-tracking apps. 4) Automate processes with custom workflows and triggers. With ClickUp API, users can streamline their project management processes and boost productivity in their organizations.

4. Name: deleteTask

Name: IPS Online
Description: Face and License Plate Anonymization
Introduction: IPS Online API (Application Programming Interface) is a powerful tool for Face and License Plate Anonymization that provides essential privacy features for any organization dealing with sensitive data. The API offers the following functions: 1) Face anonymization for images, videos, and streams. 2) License Plate anonymization for images and videos. The API returns data with well-established protocols for information security and privacy, ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. With IPS Online, users can rest assured that their data is secure and anonymized.
Functions:
1. Name: anonymizeFace
Description: Anonymizes a face in an image, video, or stream.
Input: {"image": "Required. String. Base64 encoded image data.", "boundingBox": "Optional. Array. [x,y,width,height] of the face bounding box."}
Output: Returns a base64 encoded image with the face anonymized.

2. Name: anonymizeLicensePlate
Description: Anonymizes a license plate in an image or video.
Input: {"image": "Required. String. Base64 encoded image data.", "boundingBox": "Optional. Array. [x,y,width,height] of the license plate bounding box."}
Output: Returns a base64 encoded image with the license plate anonymized.

3. Name: getBoundingBoxes
Description: Retrieves the bounding boxes of all faces or license plates in an image or video.
Input: {"image": "Required. String. Base64 encoded image data.", "type": "Required. String. 'face' or 'licensePlate'."}
Output: Returns an array of bounding boxes in the format [x,y,width,height].

4. Name: searchFaces
Description: Searches for faces in a database and returns the closest matches.
Input: {"image": "Required. String. Base64 encoded image data.", "databaseId": "Required. String. ID of the face database to search.", "maxResults": "Optional. Integer. Maximum number of results to return. Default is 10.", "threshold": "Optional. Float. Threshold for face similarity. Default is 0.6."}
Output: Returns an array of face IDs and similarity scores in the format [{"faceId": "123", "score": 0.8}, {"faceId": "456", "score": 0.7}, ...].

5. Name: addFaceToDatabase
Description: Adds a face to a database.
Input: {"image": "Required. String. Base64 encoded image data.", "databaseId": "Required. String. ID of the face database to add the face to.", "faceId": "Optional. String. ID of the face. If not provided, a unique ID will be generated.", "metadata": "Optional. Object. Additional metadata for the face."}
Output: Returns the ID of the added face.

6. Name: deleteFaceFromDatabase
Description: Deletes a face from a database.
Input: {"databaseId": "Required. String. ID of the face database to delete the face from.", "faceId": "Required. String. ID of the face to delete."}
Output: Returns a success message.

Name: Coinbase Pro
Description: Cryptocurrency Trading Platform
Introduction: Coinbase Pro API is a powerful tool for traders and developers alike that allows them to access Coinbase Pro's robust trading platform programmatically. This API offers a number of functions to help users integrate their own applications with Coinbase Pro's trading platform, including: 1) Getting account information such as balances and transaction history. 2) Placing orders and managing open orders. 3) Accessing market data such as order books, ticker prices, and historical data. With this API, users can create and execute their own trading strategies, track their portfolio performance, and develop customized tools to enhance their trading experience on Coinbase Pro.
Functions:
1. Name: Get Account
Description: Retrieves account information for the specified account ID.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- id: String. The account ID to retrieve information for.
Output: JSON object with the following fields:
- id: String. The account ID.
- currency: String. The currency of the account.
- balance: String. The current balance of the account.
- available: String. The amount of funds available to withdraw or trade.
- hold: String. The amount of funds on hold for open orders or pending withdrawals.

2. Name: List Accounts
Description: Retrieves a list of all accounts associated with the API key.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following fields:
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of accounts to return. Default is 100, maximum is 1000.
- before: String. The account ID to return accounts before.
- after: String. The account ID to return accounts after.
Output: JSON array of account objects, each with the following fields:
- id: String. The account ID.
- currency: String. The currency of the account.
- balance: String. The current balance of the account.
- available: String. The amount of funds available to withdraw or trade.
- hold: String. The amount of funds on hold for open orders or pending withdrawals.

3. Name: Place Order
Description: Places a new order on the specified product.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- product_id: String. The product ID to place the order on.
- side: String. The order side, either "buy" or "sell".
- type: String. The order type, either "limit", "market", "stop", or "stop_limit".
- size: String. The amount of the product to buy or sell.
- price: String. The price per unit of the product for limit and stop_limit orders.
- stop: String. The stop price for stop and stop_limit orders.
- client_oid: String. A unique identifier for the order. Optional.
- stp: String. The self-trade prevention flag. Optional.
- time_in_force: String. The time in force for the order, either "GTC" (good till cancelled), "GTT" (good till time), "IOC" (immediate or cancel), or "FOK" (fill or kill). Optional.
- cancel_after: String. The time after which the order should be cancelled. Optional.
Output: JSON object with the following fields:
- id: String. The order ID.
- product_id: String. The product ID the order was placed on.
- side: String. The order side.
- type: String. The order type.
- size: String. The amount of the product bought or sold.
- price: String. The price per unit of the product for limit and stop_limit orders.
- status: String. The order status, either "open", "pending", "active", "done", or "cancelled".
- created_at: String. The time the order was created.
- fill_fees: String. The total fees paid for all fills of the order.
- filled_size: String. The total amount of the product filled.
- executed_value: String. The total value of the product filled.

4. Name: Cancel Order
Description: Cancels the specified order.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- id: String. The order ID to cancel.
Output: JSON object with the following fields:
- id: String. The order ID.
- product_id: String. The product ID the order was placed on.
- side: String. The order side.
- type: String. The order type.
- size: String. The amount of the product bought or sold.
- status: String. The order status, either "open", "pending", "active", "done", or "cancelled".
- created_at: String. The time the order was created.
- fill_fees: String. The total fees paid for all fills of the order.
- filled_size: String. The total amount of the product filled.
- executed_value: String. The total value of the product filled.

5. Name: Get Product Order Book
Description: Retrieves the order book for the specified product.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- product_id: String. The product ID to retrieve the order book for.
- level: Integer. The order book level to retrieve, either 1, 2, or 3. Default is 1.
Output: JSON object with the following fields:
- sequence: Integer. The current sequence number of the order book.
- bids: JSON array of bid objects, each with the following fields:
  - price: String. The bid price.
  - size: String. The bid size.
  - order_id: String. The ID of the order that placed the bid.
- asks: JSON array of ask objects, each with the following fields:
  - price: String. The ask price.
  - size: String. The ask size.
  - order_id: String. The ID of the order that placed the ask.

6. Name: Get Product Ticker
Description: Retrieves the ticker for the specified product.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- product_id: String. The product ID to retrieve the ticker for.
Output: JSON object with the following fields:
- trade_id: Integer. The ID of the last trade.
- price: String. The price of the last trade.
- size: String. The size of the last trade.
- bid: String. The highest bid price.
- ask: String. The lowest ask price.
- volume: String. The 24 hour trading volume.

7. Name: Get Product Trades
Description: Retrieves the trades for the specified product.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- product_id: String. The product ID to retrieve the trades for.
- limit: Integer. The maximum number of trades to return. Default is 100, maximum is 1000.
- before: String. The trade ID to return trades before.
- after: String. The trade ID to return trades after.
Output: JSON array of trade objects, each with the following fields:
- time: String. The time the trade occurred.
- trade_id: Integer. The trade ID.
- price: String. The price of the trade.
- size: String. The size of the trade.
- side: String. The side of the trade, either "buy" or "sell".

Introduction: Azure DevOps is a platform that provides developers with tools to manage their software development life cycle. The Azure DevOps REST API is a set of services that allow developers to interact with different parts of Azure DevOps. The API provides the following functions: 1) Create and manage work items such as bugs, tasks, and user stories. 2) Manage and automate builds and releases. 3) Control access to resources and track user activity. 4) Manage and deploy code using repositories. These functions are provided through a series of request and response pairs which can be integrated with various programming languages and tools.

Name: Systembolaget
Description: Govornment owned liqour store in Sweden
Introduction: The Systembolaget API is a powerful tool designed to offer access to Sweden's government-owned liquor store data. Users can leverage this API to access vast catalogs of Systembolaget products, browse available alcohol categories, search for specific beverages, and retrieve detailed product information including price, alcohol content, and volume. This API simplifies the user experience of integrating Systembolaget data into any applications' advanced functionality. It provides the following features: 1) Access to a vast collection of alcohol products. 2) Structured access to categorized alcohol products. 3) Ability to perform tailored and advanced queries.
Functions:
1. Name: getProductById
Description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific product by its ID.
Input: Required. Integer. The ID of the product to retrieve.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing detailed information about the product, including its name, price, volume, alcohol content, and category.

2. Name: searchProducts
Description: Searches for products based on specified search criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object containing search criteria. The object should include the following keys:
- query: String. The search query.
- category: Optional. String. The category to search within.
- limit: Optional. Integer. The maximum number of results to return.
- offset: Optional. Integer. The number of results to skip before returning.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of products that match the search criteria. Each product object contains detailed information about the product, including its name, price, volume, alcohol content, and category.

3. Name: getCategories
Description: Retrieves a list of all available alcohol categories.
Input: None.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of category objects. Each category object contains the category's name and ID.

4. Name: getCategoryById
Description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific category by its ID.
Input: Required. Integer. The ID of the category to retrieve.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing detailed information about the category, including its name and a list of products within the category.

5. Name: getProductsByCategory
Description: Retrieves a list of products within a specific category.
Input: Required. Integer. The ID of the category to retrieve products from.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing an array of products within the specified category. Each product object contains detailed information about the product, including its name, price, volume, alcohol content, and category.

Name: Fed Treasury
Description: U.S. Department of the Treasury Data
Introduction: The Fed Treasury API (Application Programming Interface) provides access to valuable financial data from the United States Department of Treasury. It includes a wide range of financial information related to federal accounts, tax collections, public debt transactions, and more. This API provides the following functions: 1) Retrieve information on federal account balances and transactions. 2) Access details on Treasury deposits and withdrawals. 3) Retrieve information on public debt transactions, including the issuance of Treasury securities. 4) Access information on tax collections and refunds. 5) Retrieve data on Federal Reserve monetary operations. The Fed Treasury API is an essential tool for businesses, financial analysts, and researchers who require accurate and up-to-date information on U.S. Treasury operations.

1. Name: getFederalAccount
    Description: Retrieve information on federal account balances and transactions.
    Input: {"accountId": "Required. String. The unique identifier for the federal account."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Account ID
        - Account Name
        - Account Type
        - Account Balance
        - Account Status
        - Transaction History (including date, description, amount, and balance)

2. Name: getTreasuryDeposits
    Description: Access details on Treasury deposits and withdrawals.
    Input: {"startDate": "Optional. String. The start date for the deposit/withdrawal search in YYYY-MM-DD format.", "endDate": "Optional. String. The end date for the deposit/withdrawal search in YYYY-MM-DD format."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Transaction Date
        - Transaction Type (Deposit or Withdrawal)
        - Transaction Amount
        - Treasury Account Symbol
        - Treasury Account Fund Symbol
        - Treasury Account Fund Type
        - Business Event Type
        - Business Event ID

3. Name: getPublicDebtTransactions
    Description: Retrieve information on public debt transactions, including the issuance of Treasury securities.
    Input: {"startDate": "Optional. String. The start date for the transaction search in YYYY-MM-DD format.", "endDate": "Optional. String. The end date for the transaction search in YYYY-MM-DD format."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Transaction Date
        - Transaction Type (Issuance, Redemption, or Net Change)
        - Security Type
        - Security Term
        - Security CUSIP
        - Security Description
        - Transaction Amount
        - Transaction Price
        - Transaction Yield

4. Name: getTaxCollections
    Description: Access information on tax collections and refunds.
    Input: {"startDate": "Optional. String. The start date for the tax collection search in YYYY-MM-DD format.", "endDate": "Optional. String. The end date for the tax collection search in YYYY-MM-DD format."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Collection Date
        - Collection Type (Individual Income Tax, Corporate Income Tax, etc.)
        - Collection Amount
        - Refund Amount

5. Name: getFederalReserveOperations
    Description: Retrieve data on Federal Reserve monetary operations.
    Input: {"startDate": "Optional. String. The start date for the monetary operation search in YYYY-MM-DD format.", "endDate": "Optional. String. The end date for the monetary operation search in YYYY-MM-DD format."}
    Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
        - Operation Date

        - Operation Amount

Name: Open Government, Italy
Description: Italy Government Open Data
Introduction: The Open Government, Italy API is a valuable resource for those looking to access government data from Italy. It provides a comprehensive range of features including access to information on various topics such as demographics, education, health, employment, and more. Some key features of the API include 1) retrieving the information on regions, provinces, and municipalities of Italy, 2) accessing datasets on public spending, 3) accessing data on social media mentions of government agencies and politicians. With easy-to-use functionality, this API makes accessing and integrating official Italian government data into your projects a hassle-free experience.
Functions:
1. Name: getRegions
Description: Retrieves a list of all regions in Italy.
Input: None
Output: Returns a JSON object containing information on all regions in Italy, including their names, codes, and population.

2. Name: getProvinces
Description: Retrieves a list of all provinces in Italy.
Input: Required. String. The code of the region for which to retrieve provinces.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing information on all provinces in the specified region, including their names, codes, and population.

3. Name: getMunicipalities
Description: Retrieves a list of all municipalities in Italy.
Input: Required. String. The code of the province for which to retrieve municipalities.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing information on all municipalities in the specified province, including their names, codes, and population.

4. Name: getPublicSpending
Description: Retrieves data on public spending in Italy.
Input: Required. String. The year for which to retrieve data.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing information on public spending in Italy for the specified year, including the total amount spent, the amount spent by category (e.g. education, healthcare, etc.), and the amount spent by region.

5. Name: getSocialMediaMentions
Description: Retrieves data on social media mentions of government agencies and politicians in Italy.
Input: Required. String. The name of the government agency or politician for which to retrieve data.
Output: Returns a JSON object containing information on social media mentions of the specified government agency or politician, including the number of mentions, the sentiment of the mentions (positive, negative, or neutral), and the platforms on which the mentions occurred.

Name: Chronicling America
Description: Provides access to millions of pages of historic US newspapers from the Library of Congress
Introduction: The Chronicling America API is an invaluable resource for researchers, historians, and anyone who wants to gain insights into the events of the past. It grants access to millions of pages of historic US newspapers from the Library of Congress, allowing developers to create applications that can help uncover patterns and trends in American history. The API provides the following functions: 1) Search newspapers by keyword, date ranges, and geographic locations. 2) Retrieve newspaper metadata, including titles, dates of publication, and page counts. 3) Retrieve full text and image data for individual newspaper pages. With these options, users can navigate through massive amounts of data and extract valuable insights into US history.

        "city": "Optional. String. The city to search in.",
        "format": "Optional. String. The format of the newspaper to search for. Valid values are 'newspaper' and 'serial'."
    }
    Output: Returns a list of newspaper metadata objects that match the search criteria. Each object contains the following information:
    {
        "title": "String. The title of the newspaper.",
        "date": "String. The date of publication in YYYY-MM-DD format.",
        "edition": "String. The edition of the newspaper.",
        "pageCount": "Integer. The number of pages in the newspaper.",
        "placeOfPublication": "String. The place of publication.",
        "publisher": "String. The publisher of the newspaper.",
        "language": "String. The language of the newspaper.",
        "id": "String. The unique ID of the newspaper.",

Name: CleanURI
Description: URL shortener service
Introduction: CleanURI is a simple and efficient URL shortener API that can process any lengthy URL into compact and manageable links. This API includes the following features for creating shortened URLs: 1) Generate alphanumeric shortened URLs with a specified length. 2) Create custom aliases for a given URL. 3) Retrieve statistics like the number of clicks, unique visitors, and location of visitors. CleanURI offers a fast and reliable way to create custom short links for social media, email campaigns, and web pages.
Functions:
1. Name: shortenURL
Description: This function generates a shortened URL for a given long URL.
Input: {"url": "Required. String. The long URL to be shortened.", "alias": "Optional. String. A custom alias for the shortened URL. Must be unique."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the shortened URL and its corresponding statistics, including the number of clicks, unique visitors, and location of visitors.

2. Name: getURLStats
Description: This function retrieves the statistics for a given shortened URL.
Input: {"url": "Required. String. The shortened URL to retrieve statistics for."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the statistics for the given shortened URL, including the number of clicks, unique visitors, and location of visitors.

3. Name: generateRandomAlias
Description: This function generates a random alphanumeric alias for a given length.
Input: {"length": "Optional. Integer. The length of the random alias to be generated. Default is 6."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the generated random alias.

4. Name: checkAliasAvailability
Description: This function checks if a given custom alias is available for use.
Input: {"alias": "Required. String. The custom alias to check availability for."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing a boolean value indicating whether the given alias is available for use.

5. Name: getAliasURL
Description: This function retrieves the long URL associated with a given custom alias.
Input: {"alias": "Required. String. The custom alias to retrieve the long URL for."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the long URL associated with the given custom alias.

Name: Open Food Facts
Description: Food Products Database
Introduction:
The Open Food Facts API is a comprehensive food products database that provides detailed information about various food products. This API offers access to data on over 1.2 million food products from around the world. With this API, users can get access to a wide range of information related to food products including their ingredients, nutritional values, additives, and allergens. The API is designed to be easy to use and provides users with several functions to help them navigate the food products database. Some of its key functions include:

1. Search - users can search for food products using various keywords such as product name, brand, or barcode.
2. Retrieve - users can retrieve detailed information about a specific food product including its ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.
3. Compare - users can compare the nutritional values of different food products to help them make informed choices.
4. Add - users can also add new food products to the database, making it an ever-expanding resource for food-related information. 

Overall, the Open Food Facts API offers a valuable resource for anyone looking for detailed information about food products.
Functions:
1. Name: searchProduct
Description: This function allows users to search for food products using various keywords such as product name, brand, or barcode.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- search_terms: String. The search terms to be used for the search.
- page: Integer. The page number of the search results to be returned.
- page_size: Integer. The number of search results to be returned per page.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- count: Integer. The total number of search results.
- products: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a food product and contains detailed information about it, such as its name, brand, ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.

2. Name: retrieveProduct
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific food product including its ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- product_id: String. The unique identifier of the product to be retrieved.
Output: JSON object with detailed information about the product, such as its name, brand, ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.

3. Name: compareProducts
Description: This function allows users to compare the nutritional values of different food products to help them make informed choices.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- product_ids: Array of strings. The unique identifiers of the products to be compared.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- products: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a food product and contains detailed information about it, such as its name, brand, ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.
- comparison: JSON object. Contains the nutritional values of each product and their differences.

4. Name: addProduct
Description: This function allows users to add new food products to the database, making it an ever-expanding resource for food-related information.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- product_name: String. The name of the product to be added.
- brand_name: String. The name of the brand of the product to be added.
- ingredients: String. The ingredients of the product to be added.
- allergens: String. The allergens of the product to be added.
- nutrition_facts: JSON object. Contains the nutritional values of the product to be added.
Output: JSON object with detailed information about the added product, such as its name, brand, ingredients, nutritional values, and allergens.

Description: Community-driven taco database
Introduction: The TacoFancy API (Application Programming Interface) is a community-driven database that provides access to a wide range of taco-related information. The API allows users to access the following functions: 1) Search for tacos by their ingredients or name. 2) Retrieve detailed information on specific tacos, including all ingredients and preparation instructions. 3) Add new taco recipes to the database. The TacoFancy API is a valuable resource for anyone searching for unique and creative taco recipes or looking to share their own recipes with others.
Functions:
1. Name: searchTacos
Description: Search for tacos by their ingredients or name.
Input: 
{
  "query": "Required. String. The search query for the taco.",
  "limit": "Optional. Integer. The maximum number of results to return. Default is 10.",
  "offset": "Optional. Integer. The number of results to skip before returning. Default is 0."
}
Output: Returns an array of taco objects that match the search query. Each taco object contains the following information:
- name: String. The name of the taco.
- ingredients: Array of strings. The ingredients used in the taco.
- recipe: String. The preparation instructions for the taco.

2. Name: getTacoById
Description: Retrieve detailed information on a specific taco by its ID.
Input: 
{
  "id": "Required. String. The ID of the taco to retrieve."
}
Output: Returns a taco object that matches the given ID. The taco object contains the following information:
- name: String. The name of the taco.
- ingredients: Array of strings. The ingredients used in the taco.
- recipe: String. The preparation instructions for the taco.

3. Name: addTaco
Description: Add a new taco recipe to the database.
Input: 
{
  "name": "Required. String. The name of the new taco recipe.",
  "ingredients": "Required. Array of strings. The ingredients used in the new taco recipe.",
  "recipe": "Required. String. The preparation instructions for the new taco recipe."
}
Output: Returns a success message indicating that the new taco recipe has been added to the database.

Name: Iconfinder
Description: Icons
Introduction: The Iconfinder API is designed to provide a vast selection of icons for developers to integrate into their projects. With this API, developers can access over 5 million icons. The Iconfinder API provides the following functions: 1) Search for icons based on various parameters such as keywords, license types, and sizes. 2) Retrieve specific information about an icon, such as its author, tags, and similar icons. 3) Download icons in various formats, sizes, and colors. With the Iconfinder API, developers can easily and efficiently find and incorporate icons into their projects.
Functions:
1. Name: searchIcons
    Description: This function allows developers to search for icons based on various parameters such as keywords, license types, and sizes.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - query: String. The search query.
        - count: Integer. The number of icons to return. Maximum value is 100.
        - offset: Integer. The number of icons to skip before starting to return results.
        - premium: Boolean. Whether to include premium icons in the search results.
        - vector: Boolean. Whether to include vector icons in the search results.
        - license: String. The license type of the icons to search for. Possible values are "free", "premium", and "both".
        - size: String. The size of the icons to search for. Possible values are "any", "small", "medium", and "large".
    Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing an icon. Each object contains the following keys:
        - id: String. The unique identifier of the icon.
        - type: String. The type of the icon. Possible values are "vector" and "raster".
        - is_premium: Boolean. Whether the icon is a premium icon.
        - tags: Array of strings. The tags associated with the icon.
        - categories: Array of strings. The categories associated with the icon.
        - raster_sizes: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a raster size of the icon and contains the following keys:
            - size: Integer. The size of the raster image.
            - formats: Array of strings. The file formats available for the raster image.
        - vector_sizes: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a vector size of the icon and contains the following keys:
            - size: Integer. The size of the vector image.
            - formats: Array of strings. The file formats available for the vector image.
        - author: JSON object. The author of the icon. Contains the following keys:
            - name: String. The name of the author.
            - website_url: String. The website URL of the author.
            - username: String. The username of the author on Iconfinder.
        - license: JSON object. The license of the icon. Contains the following keys:
            - type: String. The type of the license.
            - url: String. The URL of the license.
        - price: JSON object. The price of the icon. Contains the following keys:
            - currency: String. The currency of the price.
            - amount: Float. The amount of the price.
            - license: String. The type of the license associated with the price.

2. Name: getIconDetails
    Description: This function allows developers to retrieve specific information about an icon, such as its author, tags, and similar icons.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
        - icon_id: String. The unique identifier of the icon to retrieve details for.
    Output: A JSON object representing the icon. Contains the same keys as the objects returned by the searchIcons function.

3. Name: downloadIcon
    Description: This function allows developers to download icons in various formats, sizes, and colors.
    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
        - icon_id: String. The unique identifier of the icon to download.
        - size: Integer. The size of the icon to download.
        - format: String. The file format of the icon to download. Possible values are "svg", "png", and "ico".
        - color: String. The color of the icon to download. Only applicable for certain icons.
    Output: The binary data of the icon file.

Name: MailboxValidator
Description: Validate email address to improve deliverability
Introduction: The MailboxValidator API is a powerful tool that allows developers to validate email addresses quickly and easily to improve email deliverability rates. With this API, you can ensure that your mailing list contains valid and current email addresses, saving you time and resources. The API provides a number of functions, including: 1) Email Validation: Verifies the existence and validity of an email address. 2) Email Verification: Checks if the email address exists and detects its type (personal, business, or disposable). 3) Disposable Email Detection: Detects disposable email addresses that are commonly used for spam. 4) Email Correction: Corrects common misspellings in email addresses to improve validity. Each function is designed to provide highly accurate results with minimal false positives, giving you a reliable tool to improve the efficiency of your email marketing campaigns.
Functions:
1. Name: Email Validation
Description: Verifies the existence and validity of an email address.
Input: {"email": "Required. String. The email address to be validated."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
- is_valid: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is valid or not.
- is_catchall: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a catch-all address or not.
- is_role: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a role-based address or not.
- is_free: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a free email address or not.
- is_mx_found: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address has a valid MX record or not.
- is_smtp_valid: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is deliverable or not.
- mailboxvalidator_score: Integer. Indicates the quality score of the email address, ranging from 0 to 100.

2. Name: Email Verification
Description: Checks if the email address exists and detects its type (personal, business, or disposable).
Input: {"email": "Required. String. The email address to be verified."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
- is_verified: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is verified or not.
- is_personal: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a personal email address or not.
- is_business: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a business email address or not.
- is_disposable: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a disposable email address or not.
- mailboxvalidator_score: Integer. Indicates the quality score of the email address, ranging from 0 to 100.

3. Name: Disposable Email Detection
Description: Detects disposable email addresses that are commonly used for spam.
Input: {"email": "Required. String. The email address to be checked for disposable status."}
Output: Returns a JSON object containing the following information:
- is_disposable: Boolean. Indicates whether the email address is a disposable email address or not.
- mailboxvalidator_score: Integer. Indicates the quality score of the email address, ranging from 0 to 100.

4. Name: Email Correction
Description: Corrects common misspellings in email addresses to improve validity.

- is_valid: Boolean. Indicates whether the corrected email address is valid or not.

Name: Twitter
Description: Read and write Twitter data
Introduction: The Twitter API (Application Programming Interface) is a set of tools that enables developers to collect and publish Twitter data. The API offers a range of functions for data retrieval and analysis, including: 1) Retrieve tweets filtered by search terms and hashtags. 2) Stream tweets in real-time. 3) Provide user and account information. 4) Access lists of followers and friends. 5) Publish tweets on behalf of a user. With Twitter API, developers can build powerful apps that interact seamlessly with Twitter's vast array of social data.
Functions:
1. Name: searchTweets
    Description: Retrieve tweets filtered by search terms and hashtags.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The search query.
        - Optional. Integer. The number of tweets to return per page. Default is 15.
        - Optional. Integer. The page number to return. Default is 1.
    Output: Returns an array of tweet objects, each containing information such as the tweet ID, text, user information, and creation date.

2. Name: streamTweets
    Description: Stream tweets in real-time.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The search query.
        - Optional. String. The language filter for the stream. Default is none.
    Output: Returns a stream of tweet objects, each containing information such as the tweet ID, text, user information, and creation date.

3. Name: getUserInfo
    Description: Provide user information.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The username of the user to retrieve information for.
    Output: Returns a user object containing information such as the user ID, name, screen name, description, location, and profile image URL.

4. Name: getAccountInfo
    Description: Provide account information.
    Input: 
        - Required. None.
    Output: Returns an account object containing information such as the account ID, name, screen name, description, location, and profile image URL.

5. Name: getFollowersList
    Description: Access a list of followers.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The username of the user to retrieve followers for.
        - Optional. Integer. The number of followers to return per page. Default is 20.
        - Optional. Integer. The page number to return. Default is 1.
    Output: Returns an array of user objects, each containing information such as the user ID, name, screen name, description, location, and profile image URL.

6. Name: getFriendsList
    Description: Access a list of friends.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The username of the user to retrieve friends for.
        - Optional. Integer. The number of friends to return per page. Default is 20.
        - Optional. Integer. The page number to return. Default is 1.
    Output: Returns an array of user objects, each containing information such as the user ID, name, screen name, description, location, and profile image URL.

7. Name: postTweet
    Description: Publish a tweet on behalf of a user.
    Input: 
        - Required. String. The text of the tweet.
    Output: Returns a tweet object containing information such as the tweet ID, text, user information, and creation date.

This API allows you to retrieve HTML content from any website and perform crawling operations with ease, all without the burden of hosting, debugging, and maintaining your own web scraping engine. The API offers the following functions: 1) Retrieving raw HTML content from any website. 2) Parsing HTML to output data in either JSON or XML format. 3) Bypassing CAPTCHAs, IP blocks, and detection algorithms. The API provides functions such as: 1) Retrieve all the music services on which a specific song is available. 2) Retrieve the URLs of the song on each of the services. 3) Determine if a song is available in your country or region. 4) Retrieve data about a particular platform or service.         - homepageUrl: String. The URL of the service's homepage.

Name: Google Drive
Description: File Sharing and Storage
Introduction: The Google Drive API is an easy and powerful way to integrate with Google Drive's file sharing and storage capabilities. With the API, you can access all of your files including documents, images, and videos, and easily create new ones from your own application. The API offers various functions such as: 1) Uploading and downloading files; 2) Searching through the files in your Drive; 3) Sharing files or folders with other users; 4) Access control and authorization for files. These functions make it easy for developers to integrate Google Drive into their applications and increase collaboration and organization.
Functions:
1. Name: uploadFile
Description: Uploads a file to Google Drive.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "file": File object to be uploaded.
- "name": String. Name of the file to be uploaded.
- "parent": String. ID of the folder where the file will be uploaded. If not provided, the file will be uploaded to the root folder.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. ID of the uploaded file.
- "name": String. Name of the uploaded file.
- "mimeType": String. MIME type of the uploaded file.
- "webViewLink": String. URL to view the uploaded file in a web browser.

2. Name: downloadFile
Description: Downloads a file from Google Drive.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "fileId": String. ID of the file to be downloaded.
Output: File object of the downloaded file.

3. Name: searchFiles
Description: Searches for files in Google Drive.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "query": String. Query string to search for files. For more information on how to construct a query, see https://developers.google.com/drive/api/guides/search-files.
- "pageSize": Optional. Integer. Number of files to return per page. Default is 100.
- "pageToken": Optional. String. Token for the next page of results. Default is null.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "files": Array of file objects that match the search query.
- "nextPageToken": String. Token for the next page of results. Null if there are no more results.

4. Name: shareFile
Description: Shares a file or folder with another user.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "fileId": String. ID of the file or folder to be shared.
- "email": String. Email address of the user to share the file or folder with.
- "role": String. Role of the user in the shared file or folder. Possible values are "owner", "writer", "commenter", and "reader". Default is "writer".
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- "id": String. ID of the permission granted.
- "role": String. Role of the user in the shared file or folder.
- "type": String. Type of the permission granted. Always "user".
- "emailAddress": String. Email address of the user the permission was granted to.

5. Name: revokeFilePermission
Description: Revokes a user's permission to a file or folder.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- "fileId": String. ID of the file or folder to revoke the permission from.
- "permissionId": String. ID of the permission to revoke.
Output: None.

Name: Food Standards Agency
Description: UK food hygiene rating data API
Introduction: The Food Standards Agency API (Application Programming Interface) is a resource that provides access to food hygiene rating data across the United Kingdom. This API allows users to access current and accurate information about restaurants, cafes, and other establishments that handle food. The functions provided by the API include: 1) Retrieving food hygiene ratings for a single restaurant or establishment. 2) Searching for food hygiene ratings for multiple establishments at once based on criteria such as postcodes or dates. 3) Retrieving information about an establishment's inspection dates, scores, and ratings. With this API, users can make informed decisions about where to eat, work, and invest, ensuring they have access to the most up-to-date food hygiene information.
Functions:
1. Name: getEstablishmentRating
Description: Retrieves the food hygiene rating for a single establishment.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- establishment_id: String. The unique identifier for the establishment.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- rating: String. The food hygiene rating for the establishment.
- rating_date: String. The date the rating was awarded.
- scores: JSON object. The scores awarded to the establishment for various categories, such as hygiene and structural compliance.

2. Name: searchEstablishments
Description: Searches for food hygiene ratings for multiple establishments based on criteria such as postcodes or dates.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- postcode: String. The postcode to search for establishments in.
- max_distance: Optional. Integer. The maximum distance in meters from the postcode to search for establishments in. Defaults to 5000 if not provided.
- business_type: Optional. String. The type of business to search for, such as "restaurant" or "cafe". Defaults to "all" if not provided.
- rating_key: Optional. String. The rating to search for, such as "5" for a rating of 5 stars. Defaults to "all" if not provided.
- rating_date: Optional. String. The date to search for ratings on, in the format "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to the current date if not provided.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- establishments: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents an establishment and has the following keys:
  - establishment_id: String. The unique identifier for the establishment.
  - name: String. The name of the establishment.
  - address: String. The address of the establishment.
  - postcode: String. The postcode of the establishment.
  - rating: String. The food hygiene rating for the establishment.
  - rating_date: String. The date the rating was awarded.

3. Name: getEstablishmentInfo
Description: Retrieves information about an establishment's inspection dates, scores, and ratings.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- establishment_id: String. The unique identifier for the establishment.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- name: String. The name of the establishment.
- address: String. The address of the establishment.
- postcode: String. The postcode of the establishment.
- ratings: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a rating and has the following keys:
  - rating: String. The food hygiene rating for the establishment.
  - rating_date: String. The date the rating was awarded.
  - scores: JSON object. The scores awarded to the establishment for various categories, such as hygiene and structural compliance.

Name: CollegeScoreCard.ed.gov
Description: Data on higher education institutions in the United States
Introduction: The CollegeScoreCard.ed.gov API is a comprehensive resource for data on higher education institutions in the United States. It provides access to information on thousands of colleges and universities, including data on cost, graduation rates, student debt, and more. The API offers the following functions: 1) Retrieval of institution-specific data on graduation rates, demographics, and programs offered. 2) Access to nationwide data on affordability and student debt. Users can refine their search by geography, institution type, and more. 3) Interactive data visualizations that provide a comprehensive analysis of higher education in the United States. With this API, users can easily access and analyze information to make informed decisions about higher education.
Functions:
1. Name: getInstitutionData
Description: Retrieves institution-specific data on graduation rates, demographics, and programs offered.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: String. The unique identification number of the institution.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- graduation_rate: Float. The graduation rate of the institution.
- demographics: JSON object with the following keys:
  - race_ethnicity: JSON object with the following keys:
    - ethnicity: String. The ethnicity of the student population.
    - percentage: Float. The percentage of the student population that identifies with the specified ethnicity.
  - gender: JSON object with the following keys:
    - male: Float. The percentage of male students at the institution.
    - female: Float. The percentage of female students at the institution.
- programs_offered: Array of JSON objects with the following keys:
  - program_name: String. The name of the program.
  - program_code: String. The code of the program.

2. Name: getAffordabilityData
Description: Retrieves nationwide data on affordability and student debt.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following keys:
- region: String. The region of the United States to filter the results by.
- institution_type: String. The type of institution to filter the results by.
- degree_type: String. The type of degree to filter the results by.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- net_price: Float. The average net price of attendance for the specified filters.
- median_student_debt: Float. The median student debt for the specified filters.

3. Name: getInteractiveVisualizations
Description: Retrieves interactive data visualizations that provide a comprehensive analysis of higher education in the United States.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following keys:
- visualization_type: String. The type of visualization to retrieve.
- filters: JSON object with the following keys:
  - region: String. The region of the United States to filter the results by.
  - institution_type: String. The type of institution to filter the results by.
  - degree_type: String. The type of degree to filter the results by.
Output: HTML code for the specified visualization.

This API is an ideal resource for developers looking to integrate the Guardian's authoritative reporting into their application. Input: {"section": "Required. String. The section to search for."}
Output: Returns an array of articles, each containing the article's ID, title, publication date, and URL.

3. Name: getArticleDetails
Description: Retrieve details for a specific article.
Input: {"articleId": "Required. String. The ID of the article to retrieve."}
Output: Returns an object containing the article's ID, title, publication date, URL, body text, and author information.

4. Name: searchArticles
Description: Search the Guardian's content for articles containing specific words or phrases.
Input: {"query": "Required. String. The search query to use."}
Output: Returns an array of articles matching the search query, each containing the article's ID, title, publication date, and URL.

5. Name: getAuthorDetails
Description: Retrieve details for a specific author.
Input: {"authorId": "Required. String. The ID of the author to retrieve."}
Output: Returns an object containing the author's ID, name, bio, and a list of articles they have written.

Name: Sirv
Description: Image management solutions like optimization, manipulation, hosting
Introduction: Sirv API is a powerful image management tool designed to optimize, manipulate and host image files for various applications. With Sirv, users can easily and efficiently manage their digital assets, making them more suitable for their end users. The API provides the following features: 1) Image optimization to reduce file size without compromising image quality. 2) Image manipulation, allowing users to crop, resize, and rotate images to fit their specific needs. 3) High-performance image hosting, providing fast image delivery for web and mobile applications. 4) Real-time image transformations, providing the flexibility to create on-the-fly image variations based on user needs. The Sirv API offers a powerful set of features that make it an ideal choice for businesses looking for efficient image management solutions.

1. Name: optimizeImage
    Description: This function optimizes an image to reduce its file size without compromising its quality.
    Input: {"image_url": "Required. String. The URL of the image to be optimized."}
    Output: The optimized image file.

2. Name: resizeImage
    Description: This function resizes an image to the specified dimensions.
    Input: {"image_url": "Required. String. The URL of the image to be resized.", "width": "Required. Integer. The desired width of the image.", "height": "Required. Integer. The desired height of the image."}
    Output: The resized image file.

3. Name: cropImage
    Description: This function crops an image to the specified dimensions.
    Input: {"image_url": "Required. String. The URL of the image to be cropped.", "x": "Required. Integer. The x-coordinate of the top-left corner of the crop area.", "y": "Required. Integer.
